verdict.rationale: Unity documents public scripting APIs and publishes a versioned API lifecycle policy for its Services Web APIs that keeps breaking changes out of existing versions, which partly supports the stable, well-documented side of the story. Nothing in the pack shows abundant public code examples or measured first-try success of LLM-generated Unity code, and the engine manual has no llms.txt or .md mirrors. missing for 10: evidence of abundant public code examples, any evidence of LLM first-try code success, stability guarantees for the engine scripting API (the lifecycle policy covers only the Services Web APIs, with short deprecation windows), machine-readable engine docs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, LLM-generated code mostly works on the first try — stable, well-documented APIs with abundant public examples the models have seen

citations.quote: Interacting directly with the public Unity APIs allows for finer control and a greater degree of customization.
Breaking changes are introduced only to new API versions.
